title: Delegate agent work input
description: Ask the daemon for a piece of agent work on a named model route (docs/model-routes.md, section 8): the request as text, the route by name, and optionally a protocol (a runbook the daemon can run), a workspace (a directory under a daemon context root, copied into the run's workspace), settings, a session and an idempotency key. A delegation is a run: the accepted outcome (delegated) creates the Run as SubmitRun does, with the request as its intake, at the daemon's default level, and the daemon writes the run's first event `runbook.submitted` (sequence 1) and its second, `runbook.delegated` (the route, the path and the protocol), before the runtime records any; cancel-run, the run views and the events work on it unchanged. With a protocol that runbook runs (path `named`); with the protocol `delegation-free`, or without one on a daemon that has no classifier route, the free run (path `free`): one agent node whose instruction is the request, on the delegation's route, in the run's workspace, writing `result.md`; its runbook is `delegation-free`, the handler fills `runbook_id` with it. Without a protocol on a daemon with a classifier route (`[route_policy] classifier`) the daemon takes the path when the run starts (docs/model-routes.md, section 9): `runbook_id` is `delegation` and RunDelegated holds no path; one call on the classifier route through the relay, with the request and the catalog of the daemon's runbooks, answers a runbook and a confidence, and at the daemon's `[delegation] classify_threshold` (0 to 1, default 0.8) or above, when that runbook takes every input the answer fills, it runs with the request as its intake (path `classified`); below it a second call writes a protocol whose every action is the daemon's agent node (`sdc-node delegation.free`), which the daemon checks with the loader of a runbook and runs (path `generated`). The run event `runbook.delegation-resolved` records the path, the protocol, the confidence, the classifier route and the digest of a generated protocol; the classifier's answer and the generated protocol are files of the run's work/ directory under `delegation/`. A call the route does not serve fails the run's start `route-unavailable: ...`, an answer that is not the JSON asked for (after two more calls that quote the validator's error) `classifier-answer: ...`, and a generated protocol the loader refuses `protocol-refused: <the loader's line>` (FailRunStart, outside this command). Every model call of the run goes to that route through the daemon's relay. The run's result is read by its id from the view DelegationResult. The handler mints the run id and fills `run_id`, `runbook_id`, `confinement`, `route`, `model_route_alias`, `model_route_source`, `daemon_id` and `at`, and reports four facts it reads from the host: `route_declared` (the route the delegation names, or the daemon's default route when it names none, is one the daemon declares), `runbook_known`, `context_inside_roots` and the size of the request (checked here). Before anything is written the handler also asks the route's gateway what a submit asks (docs/model-routes.md, section 3: `GET /ready`, `GET /v1/models`, the status of the route's model): a gateway that is not ready or does not answer refuses the delegation with 503 `route-unavailable` naming the route, the daemon's `{refused, message}` answer, outside the language as a draining daemon's refusal is; an alias the gateway does not list refuses it `route-refused`; a model that cannot answer yet leaves the run waiting for its route (WaitForRoute) as a submitted run waits. A delegation whose path is still open (it names no protocol on a daemon with a classifier route) is read with the classifier route as well: no classify call goes to that route before it can answer.

request.description: The work asked for, as text: the run's intake, at most 1 MiB.

model_route.description: The route the run's model calls take, by the name the daemon declares it under; absent: the daemon's default route, and a daemon with none refuses the delegation as route-refused. Never an address, a token or an alias.

protocol.description: The runbook to run with the request as its intake, or delegation-free for the free run; absent: the daemon classifies the request when it has a classifier route, else the free run.

workspace.description: A directory under one of the daemon's context roots: its files are copied into the run's workspace before the run starts.

caller.description: Who asked: the name the MCP client gave in initialize (clientInfo.name), at most 200 characters. `runbook mcp` fills it; it is no argument of the MCP tool. Recorded in the run event `runbook.delegated`.

caller_label.description: The label of the session that asked (RUNBOOK_CALLER of the session `runbook mcp` serves), at most 200 characters. `runbook mcp` fills it; it is no argument of the MCP tool. Recorded in the run event `runbook.delegated`.

runbook_id.description: The runbook the run takes: the protocol; delegation-free for the free run; delegation for a delegation the daemon classifies when its run starts. The handler fills it.

confinement.description: The daemon's default level: a delegation names none. The handler fills it; a daemon with no default refuses the delegation by name (400) and writes nothing.

route.description: The route the run takes, by name: model_route, else the daemon's default route. The handler fills it.

model_route_alias.description: The alias of route at its gateway, as the daemon's file declares it. The handler fills it.

model_route_source.description: run when the delegation named its route, default when it took route_policy.default. The handler fills it.

path.description: named when the delegation names a runbook, free for the free run; absent for a delegation the daemon classifies when its run starts. The handler fills it.

sdc.daemon.ConfinementLevel.title: ConfinementLevel
sdc.daemon.ConfinementLevel.description: How strongly a run is sandboxed, weakest first: the runtime's names. local is not confined; linux is. oci and pod are the runtime's planned levels and are not in the set until it offers them. A submit that names no level runs at the daemon's default level (runbook serve --default-confinement, or `confinement` of runbook.toml); a daemon with none refuses the submit by name and writes nothing, as the binary has no built-in default; the handler fills it. The daemon's floor is linux unless it is started lower; the default is never below the floor, and a daemon whose default is below its floor does not start. local must be asked for by name or set as the default, and is refused under a linux floor.

sdc.daemon.ContextPath.title: ContextPath
sdc.daemon.ContextPath.description: A directory on the daemon's host, given as an absolute path. The daemon accepts it only when it lies under one of its context roots (runbook serve --context-root <dir>, repeatable; none given means no context from a path), and copies it into the run's workspace before the run starts.

sdc.daemon.DaemonId.title: DaemonId
sdc.daemon.DaemonId.description: The id of the one daemon the specification describes: the configuration row it holds is keyed by it. The HTTP handler fills it; one process is one daemon.

sdc.daemon.DelegationPath.title: DelegationPath
sdc.daemon.DelegationPath.description: How a delegation became a run (docs/model-routes.md, section 9): named (it named a protocol, and that runbook runs with the request as its intake), free (the free run, one agent node whose instruction is the request, writing result.md: asked for by the protocol delegation-free, or taken by a delegation that names no protocol on a daemon without a classifier route), classified (it named none, and one call on the classifier route picked a runbook of the daemon at or above the threshold of confidence, 0.8) or generated (the classifier's confidence was below it, and one call on the classifier route wrote a protocol of the daemon's parts, which the loader accepted).

sdc.daemon.IdempotencyKey.title: IdempotencyKey
sdc.daemon.IdempotencyKey.description: Optional text, at most 200 characters, unique per daemon, that a client sends to retry a submit safely: a second submit with a key already used returns the first run and creates none.

sdc.daemon.RouteName.title: RouteName
sdc.daemon.RouteName.description: The name of a model route the daemon declares (a table [routes.<name>] of its runbook.toml): one to 64 characters of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`. A client names a route by it, never by an address, a token or an alias; the address, the token file and the prices stay in the daemon's file.

sdc.daemon.RouteSource.title: RouteSource
sdc.daemon.RouteSource.description: The setting that chose a run's route: run (the submit named it, `model_route` or `model_routes.<role>`) or default (the submit named none and the daemon's `route_policy.default` applied; a daemon whose file declares no route but a lone `[gateway]` table and a model decider declares the interim route `default` on that gateway and takes it as its default, so a model run that names none says default too). The protocol's own word comes with its story.

sdc.daemon.RunId.title: RunId
sdc.daemon.RunId.description: The id of a run. The daemon mints it (a UUID, version 7) in the HTTP handler and returns it in the answer to the submit; the handler fills the `run_id` input of SubmitRun and a client never chooses it. The state directory of the run is named after it. A run id that is already taken cannot occur, because the daemon mints it; the specification has no refusal for it.

sdc.daemon.RunSettings.title: RunSettings
sdc.daemon.RunSettings.description: The settings of a run: a map from text to text (runbook run --set key=value), kept as written. Typed members come with the runtime's run-settings story; none are declared now.

sdc.daemon.RunbookId.title: RunbookId
sdc.daemon.RunbookId.description: The name of a runbook: a preset (sdc, sdc-bugfix) or the name of a runbook in the daemon's --runbook-dir.

sdc.daemon.SessionId.title: SessionId
sdc.daemon.SessionId.description: The name of a session, chosen by the client that opens it.
